This is due to standards committees throughout the world discussing, determining and evaluating the key conditions responsible for signal propagation along the low voltage distribution cable (LVDN) and considering other parameters and the quality of cables used for this type of communication. This paper gives some insight into the work of the committees the problems they are debating and the way to evaluate cardinal parameters to establish a seamless communication system for wire-line communications systems.

articleTitle: Design methodology for powerline coupling circuit: a system-level and Monte Carlo simulation based approach
publicationTitle: International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications, 2005.
abstract: Robust design of powerline carrier communication (PLCC) system is essential due to great advances in utilization of PLCC technology across diverse applications. Powerline communication system design is complicated by noise conducted by the media and variable channel loss and signal propagation. The coupling circuit is a critical element of a PLCC system. Traditional methods for robust design, such as Monte Carlo, may require performing prohibitive number simulations. This paper proposes a computationally efficient, system-level response surface modeling (SRSM) method for the robust design of coupling circuit and PLCC system. The SRSM method is fully automated and its performance can be directly compared with the Monte Carlo simulation method. The results obtained agree closely with those of traditional Monte Carlo method, while significantly reducing the required number of simulations.

articleTitle: Channel modeling for and performance of contactless power-line data transmission
publicationTitle: International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, we describe the modeling of the contactless power-line data transmission for the industrial decentralized transportation system, as well as the performance of the data transmission. Compared with conventional in door PLC channels [M. Zimmer et al., 2002] [K. Dostert, 2000] the channel in the decentralized transportation system has several different features, which affects the performance of the data transmission. We have achieved to transfer the data with 450 kbit/s and control one transporter remotely. In the first section of this paper, the contactless data transmission and its system components are briefly reviewed. In the second section, the equivalent circuit model of the communication channel is presented and the parameters are estimated. In the third section, the performance of the data transmission is to be presented and analyzed.

articleTitle: Protocol to avoid noise in power line networks
publicationTitle: International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications, 2005.
abstract: This paper reviews established methods of communication using in-building power conductors with particular attention to the 100 kHz to 450 kHz frequency range. Measurements have shown that noise bursts on powerline conductors occur at regular times during the 60 Hz cycle and it was observed that transmission bit errors coincide with these noise bursts. The paper describes an adaptive transmission protocol whereby transmission is suspended during periods of high interference and then continues during quiet intervals. In an experimental implementation in a commercial office environment, throughput was measured at about 80% of the nominal modem rate.

articleTitle: Power line carrier communications for center pivot irrigation control
publicationTitle: International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications, 2005.
abstract: A distributed control network was developed to control automated irrigation systems for implementing precision agriculture management concepts. This paper describes experiences with implementing three power line carrier communications (PLCC) technologies since 1995 for linear and center pivot automatic agricultural sprinkler systems. Experiences with two additional technologies are also discussed but have not been implemented in the field. The power line characteristics are investigated to show why the power distribution method is favorable to power line carrier communications regardless of loading and switching of loads for speed and direction control. The PLCC connected nodes mounted on the moving center pivot lateral also function as bridges to a wireless network that allows communications with sensors distributed around the field. A protocol that can be used with power line carrier adds flexibility and provides connectivity to nodes not accessible over the power line.

articleTitle: General chair
